newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican rand touches 4.40, fresh 6-1/2 month high.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican rand touches 4.40, fresh 6-1/2 month high.

text.p: The South African rand strengthened to 4.40 against the dollar in after hours trade on Monday -- its strongest level since July 23 last year.
Shortly after 1500 GMT, the rand was quoted at 4.4020/4050 against the dollar after touching 4.4000/4030 at 1446 GMT from 4.4385/4415 on Friday.
Dealers said the currency had been buoyed on the day by far-better-than-expected gold and foreign exchange reserves data on Friday.
The data showed the Reserve Bank's reserves increased 1.457 billion rand in January to 11.76 billion rand.
Other factors which boosted sentiment on the day were President Nelson Mandela's opening of Parliament address on Friday and strength on the domestic gilts market.
The currency has now strengthened around 30 cents since the beginning of the year.
Last year it depreciated by 29 percent against the U.S. unit.
